judged_text: The only spec added for the new controller asserts ancestry (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController); no spec in the diff posts to create, update, or destroy, so the blank-category fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, the render_json_error path, and the unguarded record lookups are never executed under test (embedding_controller_spec.rb is likewise ancestry-only). The nil-record 500s and the malformed-payload 500s in this controller ship completely unverified — the first request spec written would have caught them — and a regression in the uncategorized fallback would silently mis-categorize every host saved without a category with no test failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Admin::EmbeddableHostsController with unguarded lookups and params access that can raise 500s: in update/destroy it does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without handling `host == nil`, so a missing record will cause `NoMethodError`. In `save_host`, it does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without checking `params[:embeddable_host]` presence, so malformed payloads can also 500. The added controller specs are ancestry-only and do not exercise these paths or the blank-category fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, so these behaviors are indeed unverified in tests.
